description.p: KWinfo shows the hardware sensors of a Linux computer in one window modelled on the Sensor Status window of HWiNFO64: temperatures, voltages, currents, fan speeds, clocks, power, usage, drive and network rates and S.M.A.R.T. data, grouped by device, with the minimum, maximum and average of each since the last reset.

ul.li: A live graph for any sensor, in its own window or in a panel beside the list
Rename, hide, recolour or stop monitoring any sensor; every choice is remembered
Alerts with desktop notifications, CSV logging, and sensor values in the system tray
CPU power, core voltages, S.M.A.R.T. data and GPU load through a small privileged helper that only reads and never writes to the hardware
Labels and compute rules from your lm-sensors configuration
Dark and light themes that follow the desktop

description.p: Motherboard sensors depend on the kernel driver for the board's monitoring chip; the installation guide explains how to find and load it.

description.p: The first release: the Sensor Status window, live graphs, the privileged helper for root-only sensors, CSV logging, alerts and tray values, as a Debian package and an AppImage.
